- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates the momentum; add 1–3% to forecast for the next 5–7 days to capture sentiment-driven acceleration.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 2nd–3rd week of the 30-day horizon; apply a 1–3% upward bias to the middle-to-late period of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth transitions; use a 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment for the 10–15 day window to capture sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is near a recent low, model often underreacts; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to reflect bullish sentiment and mean reversion toward higher levels.
